newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 16.48 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 16.48 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 51 basis points to 16.48 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 50 billion bolivars of 180- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 16.99 percent coupon for a price of 100.24 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 16.99 percent.

The bank also sold 20 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 17.34 percent coupon at a price of 99.04 percent, and 20 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 17.70 percent coupon at an average price of 98.42 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 54 basis points to 18.81 percent for the 269-day bills, and 70 basis points to 19.60 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
